passages.text: Azara serrata, the saw-toothed azara, is a species of flowering plant in the family Salicaceae. It is endemic to Chile. It is an evergreen shrub growing to {{convert|4 |m|ft|abbr=on}}, with glossy serrated leaves and clusters of scented yellow flowers in summer. In temperate regions it requires a sheltered position.

Two varieties are accepted:
Azara serrata var. fernandeziana {{small|(Gay) Reiche}} – Juan Fernández Islands
Azara serrata var. serrata – central and southern Chile
This species has gained the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.
